$doc: Vyomi capability registry — Azure App Configuration. See aws/s3.json for the contract.

azure.appconfiguration.store.crud.title: Configuration stores (create, get, list, delete, soft delete/recover/purge) over ARM

azure.appconfiguration.access_keys.title: Access settings: access keys (listKeys, regenerateKey)
limitations: Enable/disable access key authentication (disableLocalAuth) is stored and returned exactly as written, and really blocks HMAC-authenticated data-plane calls once set — but Vyomi has no signed-in-identity/session-principal concept behind a data-plane call, so a store with access keys disabled cannot be reached by any other credential either (real App Configuration would fall back to Microsoft Entra ID).

azure.appconfiguration.kv.crud.title: Configuration explorer: key-values (get, list, create, update, delete, labels, tags, revisions, snapshots)

azure.appconfiguration.feature_flags.title: Feature manager (feature flags)
limitations: Feature flags are Vyomi's UI convention over plain key-values (the reserved `.appconfig.featureflag/` key prefix and the `application/vnd.microsoft.appconfig.ff+json` content type, exactly as real App Configuration stores them) — there is no dedicated feature-flag engine, so malformed flag JSON is stored and round-tripped as-is rather than schema-validated like the real service does.

azure.appconfiguration.replicas.title: Geo-replication (replicas)
limitations: A replica is a real ARM child resource with its own endpoint, but key-value reads/writes against a replica's endpoint are not modelled separately — Vyomi has one data-plane relay per store (see azure.appconfiguration.kv.crud), not one per replica, so there is nothing to simulate region-local latency or replication lag with.

azure.appconfiguration.networking.title: Networking (public network access)
limitations: publicNetworkAccess=Disabled is ENFORCED: every data-plane request (read or write) returns 403 Forbidden while the control plane stays reachable. Vyomi has no private-link network path, so private endpoints are stored but cannot restore access — every caller counts as public.

azure.appconfiguration.locks.title: Resource locks (Microsoft.Authorization/locks), scoped to this configuration store
limitations: Locks are only simulated at the resource scope (this configuration store); subscription- and resource-group-scoped lock lists are an honest 'Not simulated' gap, same as every other Azure resource blade's scope-switch buttons.

azure.appconfiguration.activity_log.title: Activity log
limitations: Only console/SDK-triggered mutations made since the simulation booted are recorded (no historical backfill), and `caller` is a fixed placeholder identity rather than the real signed-in principal. Severity/category filtering is not modelled (every recorded event is Informational/Administrative).

The Timespan picker IS enforced: its lower bound is a real OData `eventTimestamp ge` predicate (core/azure_arm_core.py _activity_log_query) — narrowing it really narrows the result, it isn't a cosmetic control.

azure.appconfiguration.iam.title: Access control (IAM)
limitations: Check access, Role assignments and Deny assignments are REAL and scoped to this configuration store's resource id: Check access runs core/azure_iam_core.py's evaluator (explicit-deny-wins, scope inheritance from the subscription/resource group), the lists filter the shared RBAC store to assignments whose scope covers it, and new assignments are created scoped to it. Principal IDs are free text (Vyomi has no real directory); 'My access' and Classic administrators stay honest gaps.
